| `RISK005` | info | A padded size lands within `±4` B of a raw WireGuard size — may confuse naive DPI. The `±4` in the message is hardcoded from the default threshold. |
| `RISK006` | warning | Junk range width is `> 0` and `< 32` B — a narrow range makes junk packets predictable. Width `0` does not fire, but that requires `Jmax < Jmin`; an all-zero range gives width `1` and fires. |
| `RISK007` | warning | Any `H1`–`H4` range width is `> 0` and `< 1 000 000` — a narrow header range reduces entropy. One finding per offending range. **Skipped entirely when header protection is active**, because `H1..H4 = 1-1/2-2/3-3/4-4` is the reference configuration. |
| `RISK008` | info | No peers are defined — I-packet analysis is skipped. |
| `RISK009` | warning | All of `S1`–`S4` and `Jc`/`Jmin`/`Jmax` are zero — the config behaves like vanilla WireGuard. |

::: tip
`RISK005` and `RISK008` are the only `info`-level analyze findings; the rest are `warning`. None are ever `error` — treat the report as a checklist to tighten obfuscation, not a pass/fail gate. Under header protection the size-based heuristics (`RISK001`–`RISK006`, `RISK009`) still apply; only `RISK007` is waived.
:::

Boundary details worth knowing:

- `RISK004` and `RISK005` require the difference to be **strictly greater than zero**, so two identical padded sizes produce no `RISK004` (whereas `validate` would report `PSC001` for that config), and a padded size exactly equal to a raw WireGuard size (e.g. `S4=32` giving `64 == WGCookieReplySize`) produces no `RISK005`, with no validator counterpart at all.
- `RISK007`'s threshold is strict: a width of exactly `1,000,000` counts as wide enough. Presets such as `lan-conservative` (`H1 [10..1000000]`, width `999,991`) do report it — but only when header protection is off.
- Junk disabled (`Jc`/`Jmin`/`Jmax` all zero) computes width `Jmax-Jmin+1 = 1`, so it yields `RISK009` **and** `RISK006` (`junk range width is 1 B — narrow range makes junk packets predictable`). The only width that does not fire is `0`, which happens solely for an inverted range (`Jmax < Jmin`).

### Report contents

The report profiles every part of the obfuscation surface.

**Text** (`--output text`) is sectioned under a `=== AmneziaWG Config Analysis ===` banner: a one-line `MTU | Port | Peers | Protocol` header, `--- Handshake Sizes ---` (`S{n} + raw = padded`), `--- Junk Packets ---` (`Jc`, range, width `Jmax-Jmin+1` or `0` when inverted), `--- Header Ranges ---` (min/max/width per `H1`–`H4`, width `0` when inverted), per-peer `--- I-Packets (per peer) ---` (snapshot, plus a `Distribution (N samples)` block when `--samples > 0`), `--- Wire Ordering ---`, an optional `--- Findings ---` section, and a closing `Note: <sample_note>`.

The ordering steps are listed as:

```text
i1 -> i2 -> i3 -> i4 -> i5
junk x <Jc>          (only when Jc > 0)
Handshake Init
```

**JSON** (`--output json`) mirrors the `AnalysisReport` structure:

> `peers`: array of `{name, snapshot{i1..i5}, distribution?{i1..i5{mean,min,max,median}, samples}}`
> `findings`: array of `Finding`
> `ordering`: `{steps: [string]}`
> `sample_note`: `I-packet sizes are freshly generated from config parameters and may differ on each run.`
> `config`: `{protocol, mtu, listen_port, peer_count}`
> `handshake`: `{init, response, cookie, transport}` each `{s_prefix, raw_size, padded}`
> `headers`: `{h1, h2, h3, h4}` each `{min, max, width}`
> `junk`: `{jc, jmin, jmax, width}`

### Examples

Snapshot analysis of the generated server config:

```shell
amnezigo analyze --config output/<server-peer>/awg0.conf
```

Distribution analysis for one peer, 200 samples, machine-readable:

```shell
amnezigo analyze --config awg0.conf --peer alice --samples 200 --output json
```

Profile QUIC-style I-packets regardless of peer settings:

```shell
amnezigo analyze --config awg0.conf --protocol quic
```

Do not rely on `--seed` for stable output (see Reproducibility above); compare runs via the distribution statistics instead.

## Findings from `generate`

`amnezigo generate` re-parses the server config it just emitted and appends `ValidateServerConfig` findings to `GenerateResult.Findings`; the CLI prints `Warnings: <n>` followed by one `OneLine()` per finding. Those findings carry no file/line (the config exists only in memory); findings that set a `key` keep it, so TRL001 renders as `[WARNING TRL001]  (key=RandomTrailers): …` (note the double space), while keyless findings such as PSC001 render as `[ERROR PSC001]: …`. Findings cover the **server config only** — client configs are never re-parsed — and only when the emitted config parses successfully. Generation ignores findings of **any** severity: an error-severity `PSC001` is still printed under `Warnings: <n>`, exits `0` and writes configs, so the list is informational. Four shipped presets emit TRL001 deliberately (see [Presets](/presets)), and the same conditions are described in the AWG 3.x reference on [Transport Protection](/transport-protection).
---
url: /library-api
---
# Library API Reference

Go API reference for `github.com/Arsolitt/amnezigo` — the declarative config-generator library that powers the `amnezigo` CLI.

## Import & overview

```go
import "github.com/Arsolitt/amnezigo"
```

The root package `amnezigo` exposes every business-logic entry point: manifest loading, the generate pipeline, obfuscation generators, the INI writer/parser, validation, analysis, presets, credential reuse, and X25519 key utilities. The `amnezigo` binary (see [CLI Reference](/cli-reference)) is a thin wrapper over `LoadManifest` → `Generate` → `ValidateServerConfig` → `Analyze`; the same calls are available to any Go program. There is no `Manager` type and no `init`/`add`/`edit`/`remove`/`export`/`list` surface — generation is driven by a single declarative manifest (see [Manifest Reference](/manifest-reference)).

The canonical flow is two calls:

```go
manifest, err := amnezigo.LoadManifest("./my-project", nil)
result, err := amnezigo.Generate(manifest, amnezigo.GenerateOptions{OutputDir: "./my-project/output"})
```

The package has no dependency on the CLI (`cobra` lives under `internal/cli`); its direct dependencies are `go-jsonnet` (manifest loading) and `golang.org/x/crypto` (key derivation), so it can be vendored into other tooling. There is no `doc.go` and no package-level doc comment, so `go doc` opens at the constant blocks — this page is the intended overview.

::: warning
Generated configs target AmneziaWG 3.1 by default (`DefaultAWGVersion`). A 3.x config is useless on a 2.0-era engine, and the 3.x layer is a superset: a key must never be emitted for a lower target version. See [Transport Protection](/transport-protection).
:::

## Generate pipeline

`Generate` is the single orchestrator. It resolves obfuscation, loads or reuses credentials, builds one server config plus one client config per client peer, and writes them to disk unless `DryRun` is set or `OutputDir` is empty.

| Symbol | Signature | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Generate` | `func Generate(manifest Manifest, opts GenerateOptions) (GenerateResult, error)` | Orchestrates the full pipeline: resolve obfuscation, load/reuse credentials, build server + client configs, and write them unless `DryRun` or `OutputDir == ""`. |
| `GenerateOptions` | `type GenerateOptions struct { ProjectDir string; OutputDir string; JpathDirs []string; PeerFilter []string; DryRun bool; FullReset bool; VPNLinks bool }` | Configures the generate pipeline: output dir, peer filter, dry-run, credential reset, and vpn:// import-link generation. `ProjectDir` and `JpathDirs` are inert. |
| `GenerateResult` | `type GenerateResult struct { ServerPeer string; Files []FileOutput; ClientPeers []string; Findings []Finding }` | Output of a generate run: server peer name, all file outputs, client peer names, and validation findings for the generated server config. |
| `FileOutput` | `type FileOutput struct { RelPath string; Content []byte }` | A single generated file: path relative to the output dir and its byte content. |
| `EncodeVPNLink` | `func EncodeVPNLink(clientINI []byte, endpoint string, listenPort int, dns []string, description string) string` | Wraps a client AWG INI config into an AmneziaVPN-app-importable vpn:// link. See [VPN Import Links](/vpn-links). |

### `Generate` pipeline steps

1. Identify the server peer (exactly 1 required, else `exactly one server peer required, found %d`).
2. Load persisted credentials from `OutputDir` (a missing output tree yields `EmptyCredentials()`, not an error).
3. Resolve obfuscation — version gates, `U16Range` normalization, the header-protection S floor, uniform S under random trailers.
4. Resolve peer credentials (reuse persisted material or generate fresh; `FullReset` discards everything).
5. Build the server config.
6. Validate the generated server config in memory (`ParseServerConfig` on the emitted bytes, then `ValidateServerConfig`) and append the findings to `result.Findings`.
7. Build client configs (sorted by name, filtered by `PeerFilter`).
8. Collect all `FileOutput` (server first, then clients alphabetically, plus optional vpn links).
9. Write files to disk when `!DryRun && OutputDir != ""`.

`Generate` is a two-pass function: every config is computed in memory first, so a build failure leaves no files behind. The write pass itself is not atomic across files — each file is created after `os.MkdirAll` and written with `os.WriteFile` mode `0600`, so a crash mid-pass can leave a partial output tree.

### `GenerateOptions` fields

| Field | Type | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `ProjectDir` | `string` | **Inert.** Stored but never read by `Generate` — the manifest is loaded separately via `LoadManifest` with its own directory argument. |
| `OutputDir` | `string` | Where configs are written as `<OutputDir>/<peer>/awg0.conf`. Empty → nothing is written and no credentials are reused (each run starts from `EmptyCredentials()`). |
| `JpathDirs` | `[]string` | **Inert.** Belongs to manifest loading: the CLI reads its own `--jpath` flags, hands them to `LoadManifest`, and also copies them into this field — but `Generate` stores and never reads it. |
| `PeerFilter` | `[]string` | When non-empty, only the named client peers are built and written; the server is always built. Unknown names are silently ignored, and persisted credentials are still loaded for every peer. |
| `DryRun` | `bool` | When `true`, configs are computed and returned in `result.Files` but never written. |
| `FullReset` | `bool` | When `true`, persisted keys are discarded and fresh credentials are generated for every peer, including a new header-protection key. |
| `VPNLinks` | `bool` | When `true`, generates an additional `<peer>/amnezigo.vpn` import-link file per client peer. See [VPN Import Links](/vpn-links). |

::: warning
`ProjectDir` and `JpathDirs` are dead options on `GenerateOptions`. Do not expect passing them to change manifest discovery or Jsonnet `jpath` resolution: call `LoadManifest(dir, jpathDirs)` (or `LoadManifestFromFile`) yourself.
:::

### `GenerateResult` fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `ServerPeer` | `string` | Name of the server peer. |
| `Files` | `[]FileOutput` | All generated files: the server config first, then client configs alphabetically; a `.vpn` file follows its client config when `VPNLinks` is set. `RelPath` is always `<peer>/awg0.conf` or `<peer>/amnezigo.vpn`, slash-joined relative to `OutputDir`. |
| `ClientPeers` | `[]string` | Names of client peers that were generated (filtered, sorted). |
| `Findings` | `[]Finding` | **Populated.** Findings come from validating the generated server config (server bytes only) — that is the count the CLI prints as `Warnings: N`. `Location.File`/`Line` are empty because the config was never a file; `Location.Key` is set only for the keyed rule codes (FLD/HDR/HPK/TRL/TRM), while collision and junk findings (PSC*/JNK001) carry no `Location` at all. |

Client configs are never re-parsed, so an issue visible only in a client config is not reported by `Generate` — point `amnezigo validate` at the file to close the gap.

### Error contract

`Generate` returns plain wrapped errors; failures are prefixed so both prefix matching and `errors.Is`/`errors.As` work.

| Error string | Raised when |
|---|---|
| `exactly one server peer required, found %d` | `Manifest.ServerPeer()` reports a count other than 1. |
| `load credentials: %w` | Reading a present output tree fails with an error other than "does not exist". |
| `resolve obfuscation: %w` | Version gates, malformed `U16Range` bounds, or the header-protection S floor fail. |
| `build server config: %w` | Server config construction fails. |
| `build client config for <peer>: %w` | A per-peer client build fails. |
| `create directory <dir>: %w` | Output directory creation fails mid-write. |
| `write file <path>: %w` | A file write fails mid-write. |

### End-to-end example

```go
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "log"

    "github.com/Arsolitt/amnezigo"
)

func main() {
    // 1. Load the manifest (".amnezigo.jsonnet" wins over "amnezigo.json").
    manifest, err := amnezigo.LoadManifest("./my-project", nil)
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatalf("load manifest: %v", err)
    }

    // 2. Generate configs in memory. DryRun keeps the tree untouched.
    result, err := amnezigo.Generate(manifest, amnezigo.GenerateOptions{
        OutputDir: "./my-project/output",
        DryRun:    true,
    })
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatalf("generate: %v", err)
    }

    fmt.Println("server peer:", result.ServerPeer)
    for _, f := range result.Files {
        fmt.Printf("  %s (%d bytes)\n", f.RelPath, len(f.Content))
    }
    for _, f := range result.Findings {
        fmt.Println(f.OneLine())
    }

    // 3. Generate only selected client peers and write them to disk.
    result, err = amnezigo.Generate(manifest, amnezigo.GenerateOptions{
        OutputDir:  "./my-project/output",
        PeerFilter: []string{"phone", "laptop"},
    })
    if err != nil {
        log.Fatalf("generate: %v", err)
    }
    fmt.Println("clients written:", result.ClientPeers)
}
```

::: warning
Credential reuse is asymmetric. `Generate` reuses only key material recovered from `OutputDir` (server/client key pairs, PSKs, the header-protection key); every obfuscation parameter the manifest leaves `nil` is re-drawn from `crypto/rand` on each call. Two `Generate` calls on an unpinned manifest produce different S/H/J values and different I-packets, while keys stay identical. Pin the obfuscation fields you care about — or set `OutputDir: ""` and treat the call as pure computation.
:::

## Manifest loading

| Symbol | Signature | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `LoadManifest` | `func LoadManifest(dir string, jpathDirs []string) (Manifest, error)` | Discovers a manifest in `dir`: `.amnezigo.jsonnet` takes precedence, then `amnezigo.json`. Returns an error if neither exists. |
| `LoadManifestFromFile` | `func LoadManifestFromFile(path string, jpathDirs []string) (Manifest, error)` | Loads a manifest from an explicit path; a `.jsonnet` suffix evaluates via the Jsonnet VM, otherwise plain JSON. |

### Discovery & evaluation rules

| Concern | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Precedence | `.amnezigo.jsonnet` is checked **before** `amnezigo.json`; if both exist, the Jsonnet file wins. |
| `jpathDirs == nil` | Defaults to `[dir/lib]` for `LoadManifest`, `[parentDir/lib]` for `LoadManifestFromFile`. |
| `.jsonnet` evaluation | Jsonnet → JSON string → parsed as `Manifest`; the `version` field is still required. No Jsonnet library ships with the project, so `lib/` is purely a user convention. See [Jsonnet](/jsonnet). |
| Version check | Both paths reject any `version` other than `1`: missing or zero → `<path>: missing or zero version field`; otherwise `<path>: unsupported schema version %d (expected 1)`. |
| Missing file | A missing manifest file is an error — unlike `LoadCredentials`, there is no empty fallback. |

::: warning
The schema-version check lives only in the loaders. A `Manifest` constructed in Go with `Version: 0` is accepted by `Generate`; only file loading enforces version 1.
:::

## Manifest types & methods

| Symbol | Signature | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Manifest` | `type Manifest struct { Peers map[string]PeerManifest; Obfuscation ObfuscationManifest; Network NetworkConfig; Version int }` | Top-level declarative config. `Version` must be `1` when loaded from a file; peer names are the map keys. |
| `NetworkConfig` | `type NetworkConfig struct { DNS []string; MTU int }` | Network-level settings shared by all peers (MTU is per-interface; DNS applies to clients). |
| `ObfuscationManifest` | see [`ObfuscationManifest` fields](#obfuscationmanifest-fields) | Obfuscation profile, including ten AWG 3.x fields: nine pointers (`*bool`/`*U16Range`) plus the `AWGVersion` string. |
| `PeerManifest` | `type PeerManifest struct { Keepalive *int; Address string; TunName string; MainIface string; Endpoint string; Protocol string; ListenPort int; DisplayName string }` | One peer; its name is the `Manifest.Peers` map key. |
| `HeaderRange` | `type HeaderRange struct { Min uint32; Max uint32 }` | Inclusive min-max range for an obfuscation header (H1–H4). |
| `(*ObfuscationManifest).HasAnyValue` | `func (o *ObfuscationManifest) HasAnyValue() bool` | Reports whether any S/H/J field is non-nil (`false` ⇒ fully random generation). |
| `(*ObfuscationManifest).ToSharedObfuscation` | `func (o *ObfuscationManifest) ToSharedObfuscation() ServerObfuscationConfig` | Copies explicit values into a `ServerObfuscationConfig`; nil fields stay zero (signal for random generation). |
| `(*PeerManifest).IsServer` | `func (p *PeerManifest) IsServer() bool` | `true` when `Endpoint != ""` **and** `ListenPort != 0`. |
| `(*Manifest).ServerPeer` | `func (m *Manifest) ServerPeer() (string, int)` | Returns the server peer name and count. A valid manifest has `count == 1`; with `count > 1` the returned name is arbitrary map order. |
| `(*Manifest).ServerPeerName` | `func (m *Manifest) ServerPeerName() string` | Returns the sole server peer name. **Panics** if count ≠ 1 — call only after validation. |
| `(*Manifest).PeerNames` | `func (m *Manifest) PeerNames() []string` | All peer names sorted alphabetically (deterministic iteration). |

### `Manifest` fields

| Field | JSON key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Peers` | `peers` | `map[string]PeerManifest` | yes | Flat peer map. Map key is the peer name (used as output directory name). |
| `Obfuscation` | `obfuscation` | `ObfuscationManifest` | no | Shared obfuscation profile; all S/H/J fields are nullable pointers. |
| `Network` | `network` | `NetworkConfig` | no | Shared interface settings (MTU, DNS). |
| `Version` | `version` | `int` | yes | Schema version; must be `1`. No `omitempty` — `{}` decodes to `0` and is rejected. |

### `NetworkConfig` fields

| Field | JSON key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `DNS` | `dns` | `[]string` | Upstream resolvers; comma-joined into `DNS =` line of client configs only. |
| `MTU` | `mtu` | `int` | Per-interface MTU; shared by server and every client. Default `1280` when 0/absent (applied at generation time, not by the loader). |

::: danger
Omitting `network.mtu` is a shipping defect: the client config then says `MTU = 1280` while I1–I5 collapse to bare `<t>` tags, because the client builder uses the raw (zero) manifest MTU before the default is applied. Always set `network.mtu` explicitly.
:::

### `ObfuscationManifest` fields

All numeric fields use pointer types to distinguish "user set to 0" from "user did not set this field". The AWG 3.x fields follow the same convention: `nil` selects the version default, an explicit `U16Range{0, 0}` disables the corresponding engine key, and `HeaderProtection`/`RandomTrailers`/`DisableCookies` default to true for the versions that support them.

| Field | JSON key | Type | Default when `nil` | Min version | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `S1` | `s1` | `*int` | random `[0,64]` (`[12,64]` under header protection) | 2.0 | S-prefix 1. An explicit `0` is **re-drawn** (`pickNonZero`), not pinned. |
| `S2` | `s2` | `*int` | random `[0,64]` (`[12,64]` under HP) | 2.0 | S-prefix 2. |
| `S3` | `s3` | `*int` | random `[0,64]` (`[12,64]` under HP) | 2.0 | S-prefix 3. |
| `S4` | `s4` | `*int` | random `[0,32]` (`[12,32]` under HP) | 2.0 | S-prefix 4. |
| `H1` | `h1` | `*HeaderRange` | generated non-overlapping range | 2.0 | Header range 1. Under HP with all four H fields unset, the constant `1-1` is used instead. |
| `H2` | `h2` | `*HeaderRange` | generated | 2.0 | Header range 2. |
| `H3` | `h3` | `*HeaderRange` | generated | 2.0 | Header range 3. |
| `H4` | `h4` | `*HeaderRange` | generated | 2.0 | Header range 4. |
| `Jc` | `jc` | `*int` | random `[0,10]` | 2.0 | Junk count. An explicit `0` survives only when `Jmin` and `Jmax` are both explicit. |
| `Jmin` | `jmin` | `*int` | random `[64,1024]` | 2.0 | Junk minimum. |
| `Jmax` | `jmax` | `*int` | random `[64,1024]`, `> Jmin` | 2.0 | Junk maximum. |
| `Protocol` | `protocol` | `string` | — | 2.0 | Decorative at manifest level — **not** consumed by generate. Only per-peer `protocol` drives I-packet shape. |
| `AWGVersion` | `awg_version` | `string` | `"3.1"` (`DefaultAWGVersion`) | 2.0 | Target generation: `"2.0"`, `"3.0"` or `"3.1"`. Any other value fails in `ParseAWGVersion`. |
| `HeaderProtection` | `header_protection` | `*bool` | `true` for `>= 3.0` | 3.0 | Enables the header-protection key. `false` removes only the `HeaderProtectionKey` line; the ranges and booleans stay. |
| `ContentPadding` | `content_padding` | `*U16Range` | `{2, 10}` | 3.0 | Content-padding addition range. `{0,0}` omits the key. |
| `RekeyAfterTime` | `rekey_after_time` | `*U16Range` | `{120, 180}` | 3.0 | Rekey-after-time seconds. |
| `RekeyTimeout` | `rekey_timeout` | `*U16Range` | `{5, 8}` | 3.0 | Rekey timeout seconds. |
| `RejectAfterTime` | `reject_after_time` | `*U16Range` | `{180, 240}` | 3.0 | Reject-after-time seconds. |
| `KeepaliveTimeout` | `keepalive_timeout` | `*U16Range` | `{8, 12}` | 3.0 | Keepalive timeout seconds. |
| `MaxHandshakeAttempts` | `max_handshake_attempts` | `*U16Range` | `{16, 20}` | 3.0 | Handshake retry budget. |
| `RandomTrailers` | `random_trailers` | `*bool` | `true` for `3.1` | 3.1 | Random-trailer mode; when on and all four S are unset, S is drawn uniformly. |
| `DisableCookies` | `disable_cookies` | `*bool` | `true` for `3.1` | 3.1 | Disables cookie replies. |

::: warning
Fields newer than the declared `awg_version` are hard errors, not ignored: `obfuscation.<field> requires awg_version <version> or later (got "<got>")`. A manifest that sets `random_trailers` while `awg_version` is `"2.0"` fails generation.
:::

### `PeerManifest` fields

| Field | JSON key | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Keepalive` | `keepalive` | `*int` | no | `PersistentKeepalive` seconds. `nil`/0 → off. |
| `Address` | `address` | `string` | yes | Interface address as CIDR. |
| `TunName` | `tun_name` | `string` | no | Server interface name; written as `#_TunName` metadata. |
| `MainIface` | `main_iface` | `string` | no | Server egress interface. When set, `PostUp`/`PostDown` iptables rules generated. |
| `Endpoint` | `endpoint` | `string` | no | `host:port`. Server marker (together with non-zero `listen_port`). |
| `Protocol` | `protocol` | `string` | no | Per-peer obfuscation protocol — this is what generate actually reads. Defaults to `quic` when empty. |
| `ListenPort` | `listen_port` | `int` | no | UDP listen port. Server marker (together with non-empty `endpoint`). |
| `DisplayName` | `display_name` | `string` | no | Displayed server name in the AmneziaVPN app when the client config is imported via a `vpn://` link. Client-peer field; ignored on the server peer. See [VPN Import Links](/vpn-links). |

### `HeaderRange` fields

| Field | JSON key | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Min` | `min` | `uint32` | Range lower bound (inclusive). |
| `Max` | `max` | `uint32` | Range upper bound (inclusive). |

Header ranges are always written two-part (`H1 = 1-1`, never `H1 = 1`), and the parser only accepts the two-part form. Only the 3.x `U16Range` keys collapse to the short `N` form.

::: tip Server-peer detection rule
A peer is a server peer iff `Endpoint != ""` **and** `ListenPort != 0`. At most one server peer is valid per manifest. `Generate` returns an error (not a panic) when the count is not exactly 1; `ServerPeerName` panics. See [Manifest Reference](/manifest-reference).
:::

## AWG version model

```go
type AWGVersion int

const (
    AWG20 AWGVersion = iota + 1 // AmneziaWG 2.0: Jc/Jmin/Jmax, S1-S4, H1-H4, I1-I5
    AWG30                       // adds HeaderProtectionKey, ContentPaddingAddition, five timer ranges
    AWG31                       // adds RandomTrailers, DisableCookies
)

const DefaultAWGVersion = AWG31
```

| Symbol | Signature | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `ParseAWGVersion` | `func ParseAWGVersion(s string) (AWGVersion, error)` | `""` (unset) → `DefaultAWGVersion`; `"2.0"`/`"3.0"`/`"3.1"` → the enum; anything else → `unsupported awg_version %q (expected "2.0", "3.0", or "3.1")`. |
| `(AWGVersion) String` | `func (v AWGVersion) String() string` | `"2.0"`, `"3.0"`, `"3.1"`; unknown values render `AWGVersion(%d)`. |

Each generation is a superset of the previous one, and an engine build rejects INI keys it does not know, so a key must never be emitted for a lower target version. Two library-side consequences matter:

- A hand-built `ServerObfuscationConfig` with the **zero** `AWGVersion` (or any value `< AWG30`) emits exactly the AWG 2.0 key set — the writer returns early below `AWG30`. Set `Version` explicitly.
- `Preset.ToServerObfuscation` hardcodes `Version: AWG31`, so every preset is 3.1 data by construction.

See [Transport Protection](/transport-protection) for the feature behind the enum.

## U16Range

```go
type U16Range struct {
    Min uint16 `json:"min"`
    Max uint16 `json:"max"`
}
```

| Symbol | Signature | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `(U16Range) IsZero` | `func (r U16Range) IsZero() bool` | `true` iff `Min == 0 && Max == 0`. |
| `(U16Range) String` | `func (r U16Range) String() string` | `"N"` when `Min == Max`, otherwise `"Min-Max"` — the engine's INI notation. |

- Type used by `ContentPaddingAddition` and the five 3.x timer parameters.
- The zero value `{0, 0}` is the unset/disabled state: the key is omitted from the emitted config and the engine keeps its default. That is distinct from an omitted manifest pointer, which selects the version default.
- Mixed zero bounds are invalid: `{"min": 0, "max": 5}` fails resolve with `obfuscation.<field>: bounds must both be zero or both non-zero` and is reported as `TRM001` in `validate`. `{0,0}` therefore cannot express "range from zero".
- Both bounds are `uint16`, so JSON values above `65535` fail to unmarshal and the parser enforces the same width with `ParseUint(..., 10, 16)`.

## Crypto / keys

| Symbol | Signature | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GenerateKeyPair` | `func GenerateKeyPair() (string, string)` | Generates an X25519 key pair with WireGuard clamping; returns `(privateKey, publicKey)` as 44-char base64. |
| `DerivePublicKey` | `func DerivePublicKey(privateKey string) string` | Derives the 44-char base64 public key from a base64 private key (applies clamping). |
| `GeneratePSK` | `func GeneratePSK() string` | Generates a 32-byte preshared key as a 44-char base64 string. |
| `GenerateHeaderProtectionKey` | `func GenerateHeaderProtectionKey() string` | Generates a 32-byte AWG 3.x header-protection key as a 44-char base64 string. Added with the 3.x work. |

### Key behavior & gotchas

| Concern | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Panic conditions | `GenerateKeyPair`, `GeneratePSK` and `GenerateHeaderProtectionKey` panic **only** on `crypto/rand` failure (`crypto: failed to generate random key: ...`). `DerivePublicKey` panics on invalid base64 or non-32-byte input. |
| WireGuard clamping | Applied before scalar multiplication in both `GenerateKeyPair` and `DerivePublicKey`: `priv[0] &= 248; priv[31] &= 127; priv[31] |= 64`. A key read back from disk is re-clamped on derivation. |
| Header-protection key | A symmetric ChaCha20 key (`device.HeaderCipherKey`), **not** a Curve25519 scalar — it must NOT be clamped, and `GenerateHeaderProtectionKey` deliberately does not clamp it. |
| Encoding | All four helpers return standard 44-character base64 (32 bytes + padding). |
| Untrusted input | Callers passing untrusted material to `DerivePublicKey` must validate first or `recover` (the unexported `tryDerivePublicKey` helper does the latter, returning `""` on any panic). |

The header-protection key is persisted in plaintext inside every config (server and clients) — treat client configs as secrets. See [Credentials & Key Reuse](/credentials).

## Obfuscation generators

| Symbol | Signature | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `GenerateSPrefixes` | `func GenerateSPrefixes(minS int) SPrefixes` | Draws S1–S3 in `[minS, 64]` and S4 in `[minS, 32]`, retrying until the four padded sizes are pairwise distinct; **panics** after 1000 attempts. The `minS` parameter is new in the 3.x work. |
| `GenerateSPrefixesWithS1` | `func GenerateSPrefixesWithS1(minS, fixedS1 int) SPrefixes` | Keeps a caller-supplied `fixedS1` and draws S2–S4 like above, requiring all six padded pairs to be distinct; panics after 1000 attempts. The fixed S1 is **not** validated. |
| `GenerateUniformSPrefixes` | `func GenerateUniformSPrefixes(minS int) SPrefixes` | Draws one value in `[minS, 32]` and returns it as `S1 == S2 == S3 == S4`. No retry loop is needed: the four padded sizes stay pairwise distinct for any S. Use under AWG 3.1 random trailers. Added with the 3.x work. |
| `SPrefixes` | `type SPrefixes struct { S1, S2, S3, S4 int }` | S-prefix bundle returned by the three generators. |
| `GenerateJunkParams` | `func GenerateJunkParams() JunkParams` | Legacy generator without collision avoidance: `Jc` in `[0, 10]`, `Jmin`/`Jmax` in `[64, 1024]` with `Jmin < Jmax`. Prefer the collision-aware variant. |
| `GenerateJunkParamsWithForbidden` | `func GenerateJunkParamsWithForbidden(forbiddenSizes [4]int) (JunkParams, error)` | Draws junk parameters whose range excludes every given size (typically the padded handshake sizes) plus the four raw WG message sizes (always checked); returns an error when the retry budget is exhausted. |
| `JunkParams` | `type JunkParams struct { Jc, Jmin, Jmax int }` | Junk parameter bundle. |
| `GenerateHeaderRanges` | `func GenerateHeaderRanges() [4]HeaderRange` | Four sorted, non-overlapping H1–H4 ranges generated above the WG type-id window `[1..4]`; panics after 1000 attempts. |
| `GenerateConfig` | `func GenerateConfig(protocol string, mtu, s1, jc int) ClientObfuscationConfig` | Full client obfuscation bundle including I1–I5, satisfying the size-classification invariant; **panics** if the generated sizes violate `ValidatePacketSizes`. |
| `GenerateServerConfig` | `func GenerateServerConfig(_, s1, jc int) ServerObfuscationConfig` | Server obfuscation without I1–I5. The first parameter is unused (historically the MTU); panics when junk-range generation exhausts its retry budget. |
| `GenerateCPS` | `func GenerateCPS(protocol string, mtu, s1, _ int) (string, string, string, string, string)` | Returns I1–I5 for a protocol template. The fourth parameter is unused and the forbidden set is empty, so there is **no** size-collision avoidance. |

`minS` is the inclusive lower bound for every generated S value: use `0` for the AWG 2.0 path and `12` (the ChaCha20 header-cipher nonce size, `headerProtectionNonceSize`) whenever header protection is active, because the engine rejects `S < 12` in that mode. The pipeline applies the same floor via `checkSPrefixFloor` and aborts with `header protection requires S1-S4 >= 12 (got S<n>=<value>)`; `GenerateSPrefixesWithS1` does not check a caller-supplied `fixedS1` against it.

::: warning
The `minS` parameter is a source-level breaking change: pre-3.x callers of `GenerateSPrefixes()` / `GenerateSPrefixesWithS1(s1)` must add the leading argument.
:::

Pipeline shortcuts worth knowing when embedding the generators:

- Under header protection with every H field unset, the pipeline writes the constant `1-1`/`2-2`/`3-3`/`4-4` ranges instead of calling `GenerateHeaderRanges`, because the 4-byte message type is encrypted. One explicit H disables the shortcut and the other three are generated.
- `GenerateHeaderRanges` always excludes `[1..4]`, even when header protection is off — a user who disables HP and leaves H unset gets wide random ranges, never the reference set.
- Uniform S is selected only when random trailers are on **and** all four S values are unset in the manifest (`uniform := randomTrailers && obf.S1 == nil && obf.S2 == nil && obf.S3 == nil && obf.S4 == nil`). Pinning one S switches the rest to independent draws and `TRL001` then fires.

See [Obfuscation](/obfuscation) for the packet-size invariant these ranges protect.

## CPS helpers

| Symbol | Signature | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `BuildCPSTag` | `func BuildCPSTag(tagType, value string) string` | Wraps one tag in angle brackets; unknown types return `""`. |
| `BuildCPS` | `func BuildCPS(tags []string) string` | Concatenates tag strings. |
| `CPSLength` | `func CPSLength(cps string) int` | On-wire byte length with the same accounting as generation-time validation — the exported byte oracle. |
| `CPSConfig` | `type CPSConfig struct { I1, I2, I3, I4, I5 string }` | The five custom packet strings. |
| `TagSpec` | `type TagSpec struct { Type, Value string }` | Spec entry inside protocol templates. |
| `I1I5Template` | `type I1I5Template struct { I1, I2, I3, I4, I5 []TagSpec }` | Template shape returned by the six template constructors. |

### Supported `BuildCPSTag` types

| `tagType` | Result | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `"b"` | `<b 0x...>` | Hex bytes; a missing `0x` prefix is added automatically. |
| `"r"` | `<r N>` | N random bytes. |
| `"rc"` | `<rc N>` | N random letters from `[a-zA-Z]` (52 characters, no digits). |
| `"rd"` | `<rd N>` | N random digits. |
| `"t"` | `<t>` | 4-byte big-endian timestamp; `value` is ignored. |
| `"d"` | `<d>` | Passthrough marker; `value` is ignored; contributes 0 bytes at generation time. |

Any other type — including the legacy kernel-only `"c"` counter tag — returns the empty string sentinel, and unknown or malformed tags count as **0 bytes** in `CPSLength` (the numeric parse error is ignored). The amneziawg-go 3.1 engine parser also accepts `ds`/`dz` tags, but no amnezigo code recognises or emits them: a hand-written `<dz 32>` silently disappears from size accounting and validation. `GenerateCPS` never emits `<d>` for `protocol: random` (a standalone random interval has no earlier interval to source it from).

For a named template the generated I1–I5 strings are deterministic: the same `protocol` and `MTU` produce identical strings for every peer and across runs. A fresh tag sequence per run happens only for `protocol: random`. On-wire bytes still differ even for identical strings, because `<r N>` and `<t>` expand in the engine at send time.

## Protocol constants & templates

The protocol template names are available as exported constants. Prefer these over bare string literals when setting `AnalyzeOptions.Protocol` or `PeerManifest.Protocol`.

| Constant | Value |
|---|---|
| `ProtocolQUIC` | `"quic"` |
| `ProtocolDNS` | `"dns"` |
| `ProtocolDTLS` | `"dtls"` |
| `ProtocolSTUN` | `"stun"` |
| `ProtocolSIP` | `"sip"` |
| `ProtocolRTP` | `"rtp"` |
| `ProtocolRandom` | `"random"` |

`ListProtocols()` (`func ListProtocols() []string`) returns all seven names sorted alphabetically: `dns`, `dtls`, `quic`, `random`, `rtp`, `sip`, `stun`. Use it to validate user-supplied protocol names. An unknown name is not rejected anywhere: it falls through to the named-template path, and `getTemplate`'s default branch picks one of the six templates at random. An empty protocol means QUIC during `Generate` but random during `Analyze`.

| Constructor | Mimics |
|---|---|
| `QUICTemplate()` | QUIC Initial long-header packet. |
| `DNSTemplate()` | DNS query. |
| `DTLSTemplate()` | DTLS 1.2 ClientHello. |
| `STUNTemplate()` | STUN binding request. |
| `SIPTemplate()` | SIP OPTIONS request (ASCII; literal fragments are `<b>` hex, variable tokens use `<rc>`/`<rd>` only). |
| `RTPTemplate()` | RTP media packet (RFC 3550 fixed header). |

Each constructor returns an `I1I5Template` whose intervals are `[]TagSpec` type/value pairs; I5 is empty for all six named templates. See [Obfuscation](/obfuscation) for the templates' measured byte budgets.

## Config types & writer/parser API

| Type | Definition | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `ServerConfig` | `struct { Peers []PeerConfig; Interface InterfaceConfig; Obfuscation ServerObfuscationConfig }` | Full server config. |
| `InterfaceConfig` | `struct { TunName, DNS, Address, PostUp, PostDown, MainIface, EndpointV6, PrivateKey, PublicKey, EndpointV4 string; MTU, ListenPort, PersistentKeepalive int; ClientToClient bool }` | Server `[Interface]` section. |
| `PeerConfig` | `struct { CreatedAt time.Time; ClientObfuscation *ClientObfuscationConfig; Name, PrivateKey, PublicKey, PresharedKey, AllowedIPs string }` | Server `[Peer]` section; `ClientObfuscation` is nil in parsed server configs. |
| `ServerObfuscationConfig` | `struct { Jc, Jmin, Jmax, S1..S4 int; H1..H4 HeaderRange; Version AWGVersion; HeaderProtectionKey string; ContentPadding, RekeyAfterTime, RekeyTimeout, RejectAfterTime, KeepaliveTimeout, MaxHandshakeAttempts U16Range; RandomTrailers, DisableCookies bool }` | Server obfuscation; a **zero** `Version` disables emission of the whole 3.x block. |
| `ClientObfuscationConfig` | `struct { I1, I2, I3, I4, I5 string; ServerObfuscationConfig }` | Client obfuscation = server block plus I1–I5. |
| `ClientConfig` | `struct { Peer ClientPeerConfig; Interface ClientInterfaceConfig }` | Full client config. |
| `ClientInterfaceConfig` | `struct { PrivateKey, Address, DNS string; Obfuscation ClientObfuscationConfig; MTU int }` | Client `[Interface]`. |
| `ClientPeerConfig` | `struct { PublicKey, PresharedKey, Endpoint, AllowedIPs string; PersistentKeepalive int }` | Client `[Peer]`. |

| Symbol | Signature | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `WriteServerConfig` | `func WriteServerConfig(w io.Writer, cfg ServerConfig) error` | Writes the server INI in canonical key order, including version-gated 3.x keys and `#_` metadata. |
| `WriteClientConfig` | `func WriteClientConfig(w io.Writer, cfg ClientConfig) error` | Writes the client INI including I1–I5 and an always-present `PersistentKeepalive` line. |
| `SaveServerConfig` | `func SaveServerConfig(path string, cfg ServerConfig) error` | Atomic single-file write: `path + ".tmp"` followed by a rename. |
| `ParseServerConfig` | `func ParseServerConfig(r io.Reader) (ServerConfig, error)` | Back-compat shim over `ParseServerConfigWithOptions` with default options; never returns warnings. |
| `ParseServerConfigWithOptions` | `func ParseServerConfigWithOptions(r io.Reader, opts ParseOptions) (ServerConfig, []ParseWarning, error)` | Full parser. In non-strict mode the warning slice is always nil; malformed 3.x values (bad `HeaderProtectionKey`, inverted H range, malformed uint16 range, bad bool) are errors. |
| `ParseOptions` | `type ParseOptions struct { Strict bool }` | `Strict` collects non-fatal anomalies — unknown INI keys (`KEY001`) and raw `<c>` literals (`CPS001`) — as warnings; structural H-range checks stay errors. |
| `ParseWarning` | `type ParseWarning struct { Message, Key, Code string; Line int }` | One non-fatal strict-parse observation. |
| `LoadServerConfig` | `func LoadServerConfig(path string) (ServerConfig, error)` | Opens a file and parses it non-strictly. |

Structural parse failures abort parsing and surface as one `PSE001` finding in the CLI; semantic problems (`HPK001`/`TRL001`/`TRM001`/`PSC*`) are findings on an otherwise parsed config. See [Validation & Analysis](/validation).

::: warning
A hand-built `ServerObfuscationConfig` with the zero `AWGVersion` emits exactly the AWG 2.0 key set. Set `Version` explicitly when writing 3.x configs by hand.
:::

## Validation

> Full rule descriptions, finding codes and CLI exit-code semantics live in [Validation & Analysis](/validation).

| Symbol | Signature | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `ValidatePacketSizes` | `func ValidatePacketSizes(s1, s2, s3, s4 int, iPacketSizes []int, jmin, jmax int) error` | Enforces the size-classification invariant: four S-padded handshake sizes pairwise distinct, no I-packet equal to a padded size, junk range excludes all padded + raw WG sizes. Checks run in that order. |
| `ValidateHeaderRange` | `func ValidateHeaderRange(r HeaderRange) error` | Rejects `Max < Min` or any inclusive range overlapping WG message type-ids `[1..4]`. |
| `ValidateServerConfig` | `func ValidateServerConfig(cfg *ServerConfig) []Finding` | Runs every rule (required fields, S-prefixes, junk range, header ranges, 3.x header-protection/trailer/range rules); empty slice = clean. Never returns an error. |
| `PaddedSizes` | `func PaddedSizes(s1, s2, s3, s4 int) [4]int` | Returns the four AWG-padded packet sizes in packet-class order: init (`s1+148`), response (`s2+92`), cookie (`s3+64`), transport (`s4+32`). |
| `Finding` | `type Finding struct { Message string; Detail string; Code string; Severity Severity; Location Location }` | One validation/analysis observation (JSON-tagged; reused by `analyze`). |
| `Finding.OneLine` | `func (f Finding) OneLine() string` | Canonical text form `[<SEVERITY> <CODE>] <file>:<line> (key=<key>): <message>` (line/key omitted when empty). |
| `Severity` | `type Severity string` | Finding impact class. |
| `Severity` constants | `SeverityError`, `SeverityWarning`, `SeverityInfo` (`"error"` / `"warning"` / `"info"`) | The three severity levels. |
| `Location` | `type Location struct { File string; Key string; Line int }` | Where a finding originates within a config file. |
| `PacketSizeCollisionError` | `type PacketSizeCollisionError struct { Kind string; Pair string; Size int }` | One `ValidatePacketSizes` collision; `Kind` ∈ `{"s-pair", "i-packet", "junk-range"}`. |
| `(*PacketSizeCollisionError).Error` | `func (e *PacketSizeCollisionError) Error() string` | Formats as `packet size collision (<kind>): <pair> at <size> bytes`. |
| `ErrEmptyJunkRange` | `var ErrEmptyJunkRange = errors.New("junk range is empty (jmin > jmax)")` | Sentinel returned by `ValidatePacketSizes` when `jmin > jmax`. |

### WG message size constants

| Constant | Value | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `WGInitiationSize` | `148` | Raw WG initiation message size (before S-padding). |
| `WGResponseSize` | `92` | Raw WG response message size. |
| `WGCookieReplySize` | `64` | Raw WG cookie reply message size. |
| `WGTransportSize` | `32` | Raw WG transport message size. |

Sourced from amneziawg-go's `device/noise-protocol.go`; used by validation to ensure junk ranges avoid real WG traffic.

### `ValidatePacketSizes` return contract

| Outcome | Return value | How to detect |
|---|---|---|
| All invariants hold | `nil` | direct check |
| `jmin > jmax` | `ErrEmptyJunkRange` | `errors.Is(err, amnezigo.ErrEmptyJunkRange)` |
| First collision (S-pairs → I-packets → junk range) | `*PacketSizeCollisionError` | `var c *amnezigo.PacketSizeCollisionError; errors.As(err, &c)` |

The caller owns the `iPacketSizes` slice, so pass everything you want checked. Generation-time acceptability (`cpsAcceptable`) skips zero entries as unset because a real CPS is at least 4 bytes, and `GenerateCPS` always passes an empty forbidden set, so it performs no collision avoidance at all.

### Library-side validation notes

- `ValidateServerConfig` calls `ValidatePacketSizes` with a nil I-packet slice, so an I-packet collision (`PSC003`) is reachable only by calling `ValidatePacketSizes` directly.
- The WG type-id rejection (`HDR001`) is suppressed whenever `HeaderProtectionKey != ""`; under header protection the reference `H1 = 1-1` … `H4 = 4-4` configuration is expected. `Max < Min` (`HDR002`) is always rejected.
- H-range **overlap** is not an amnezigo validation rule at all — the engine rejects it at `awg setconf` time (`headers must not overlap`).
- The 3.x rule codes surfaced through this API are `HPK001` (S < 12 with header protection), `HPK003`, `TRL001` (random trailers with unequal S) and `TRM001` (half-zero `U16Range`) — catalogued in [Validation & Analysis](/validation).

## Analysis

`Analyze` is informational: it profiles a server config and emits only `warning`/`info` findings (never `error`), so the CLI `analyze` command always exits 0.

| Symbol | Signature | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Analyze` | `func Analyze(cfg ServerConfig, opts AnalyzeOptions) AnalysisReport` | Produces an `AnalysisReport`; I-packets are freshly generated from the config (not read from disk). Never returns an error. |
| `AnalyzeOptions` | `type AnalyzeOptions struct { Rand io.Reader; Protocol string; PeerName string; Samples int }` | Configures analysis: protocol template, peer filter (empty ⇒ all), sample count. `Rand` is dead. |
| `AnalysisReport` | `type AnalysisReport struct { Peers []PeerProfile; Findings []Finding; Ordering OrderingDesc; SampleNote string; Config ConfigInfo; Handshake HandshakeProfile; Headers HeaderProfile; Junk JunkProfile }` | Top-level output: config metadata, handshake/junk/header profiles, per-peer I-packet analysis, wire ordering, and heuristic findings. |
| `FormatText` | `func FormatText(report AnalysisReport) string` | Renders a report as human-readable multi-section text. |
| `FormatJSON` | `func FormatJSON(report AnalysisReport) (string, error)` | Renders a report as indented JSON (two spaces); wraps marshal errors with `%w`. |
| `ListProtocols` | `func ListProtocols() []string` | Returns alphabetically-sorted protocol template names (`dns`, `dtls`, `quic`, `random`, `rtp`, `sip`, `stun`). Use to validate user-supplied protocol names or enumerate available templates. |

### `AnalyzeOptions` fields

| Field | Type | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `Rand` | `io.Reader` | **Dead field — a shipping defect.** It is declared as the randomness source for CPS generation but no package code path reads it; I-packet generation always uses `crypto/rand`. Passing a seeded reader changes nothing and reports stay non-deterministic. |
| `Protocol` | `string` | Empty ⇒ `"random"` (`ProtocolRandom`). Accepted values: `random`, `quic`, `dns`, `dtls`, `stun`, `sip`, `rtp` — see [Protocol constants](#protocol-constants--templates). Unknown names are not rejected; they fall through to a randomly chosen named template. |
| `PeerName` | `string` | Empty ⇒ analyze all peers. |
| `Samples` | `int` | `0` ⇒ snapshot-only (one `PeerSnapshot` per peer). `> 0` ⇒ distribution mode with `Stats` over N samples. |

### Report sub-types

| Type | Fields | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `ConfigInfo` | `Protocol string`, `MTU int`, `ListenPort int`, `PeerCount int` | Basic config metadata. |
| `HandshakeProfile` | `Init`, `Response`, `Cookie`, `Transport` (all `PaddedSize`) | The four S-padded handshake sizes. |
| `PaddedSize` | `SPrefix int`, `RawSize int`, `Padded int` | One padded size entry. |
| `JunkProfile` | `Jc int`, `Jmin int`, `Jmax int`, `Width int` | Junk parameters and range width. |
| `HeaderProfile` | `H1`, `H2`, `H3`, `H4` (all `HeaderRangeInfo`) | The four H-ranges. |
| `HeaderRangeInfo` | `Min uint32`, `Max uint32`, `Width uint32` | One header range. |
| `PeerProfile` | `Name string`, `Snapshot PeerSnapshot`, `Distrib *PeerDistrib` | Per-peer I-packet analysis. |
| `PeerSnapshot` | `I1`, `I2`, `I3`, `I4`, `I5 int` | One generation of the five I-packet sizes. |
| `PeerDistrib` | `I1`–`I5` `Stats`, `Samples int` | Distribution stats over N samples. |
| `Stats` | `Mean float64`, `Min int`, `Max int`, `Median int` | Summary statistics. |
| `OrderingDesc` | `Steps []string` | Packet ordering on the wire per handshake. |

The report's `SampleNote` states that I-packet sizes are freshly generated from config parameters and may differ on each run — `Analyze` ignores the I1–I5 strings stored in the config file.

### Heuristic finding codes

`Analyze` populates `Finding.Code` with the following string values. **They are string codes, not exported Go constants** — match them by string value.

| Code | Severity | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `RISK001` | warning | Junk range contains a raw WG size. |
| `RISK002` | warning | A peer's I-packet cluster spans < 20 B. |
| `RISK003` | warning | `S4 < 8`. |
| `RISK004` | warning | Two padded sizes differ by < 5 B. |
| `RISK005` | info | A padded size is within ±4 B of a raw WG size. |
| `RISK006` | warning | Junk range width < 32 B. |
| `RISK007` | warning | An H-range width < 1,000,000 — **skipped entirely when header protection is active**. |
| `RISK008` | info | No peers defined. |
| `RISK009` | warning | All S-prefixes and junk params are zero (vanilla-WG shape). |

## Presets

> Preset values and selection guidance live in [Presets](/presets).

```go
type Preset struct {
    Name            string
    Description     string
    DefaultProtocol string
    H1, H2, H3, H4  HeaderRange
    MTU             int
    S1, S2, S3, S4  int
    Jc, Jmin, Jmax  int

    // AWG 3.x additions.
    ContentPadding U16Range
    RandomTrailers bool
    DisableCookies bool
}
```

| Symbol | Signature | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `Preset` | see above | A named bundle of obfuscation parameters; each yields a config that passes `ValidatePacketSizes`. There is no `Preset.Version` field — presets are AWG 3.1 data by construction. |
| `Preset.ToServerObfuscation` | `func (p Preset) ToServerObfuscation() ServerObfuscationConfig` | Converts a preset to a `ServerObfuscationConfig`. Copies `Jc`/`Jmin`/`Jmax`, `S1`–`S4`, `H1`–`H4` and the three 3.x fields, hardcodes `Version: AWG31`, and leaves `HeaderProtectionKey` **empty** on purpose (the pipeline supplies the key separately). Drops `Name`, `Description`, `DefaultProtocol` and `MTU`. |
| `GetPreset` | `func GetPreset(name string) (Preset, error)` | Returns the named preset; on unknown names returns `unknown preset %q; available presets: %v` (Go-style registry slice). |
| `ListPresets` | `func ListPresets() []Preset` | Returns a defensive copy of all seven built-in presets. |

The seven built-in presets: `lan-conservative`, `home-balanced`, `mobile-aggressive`, `stealth-paranoid`, `standard-1420`, `low-overhead`, `test-minimal`. There is no `preset` field in `Manifest`; to use a preset, copy its values into `ObfuscationManifest` (or evaluate it at the Jsonnet layer). Four presets (`home-balanced`, `mobile-aggressive`, `stealth-paranoid`, `standard-1420`) pin unequal S values with `RandomTrailers` on, so copying them verbatim makes `generate` report `TRL001`.

::: warning
Because `ToServerObfuscation` leaves `HeaderProtectionKey` empty and the writer omits an empty key, writing that config directly yields a 3.1 config **without** header protection. See [Transport Protection](/transport-protection).
:::

## Credentials

> Key-reuse model and recovery sources are documented in [Credentials & Key Reuse](/credentials).

| Symbol | Signature | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `PeerCredentials` | `type PeerCredentials struct { PrivateKey string; PublicKey string; PresharedKey string }` | Cryptographic material for one peer: base64 X25519 private key, derived public key, and a per-connection PSK. |
| `PersistedCredentials` | `type PersistedCredentials struct { Peers map[string]PeerCredentials; Server PeerCredentials; HeaderProtectionKey string }` | All credentials extracted from existing output configs; reused by `Generate` across runs. `HeaderProtectionKey` is the 3.x addition. |
| `EmptyCredentials` | `func EmptyCredentials() *PersistedCredentials` | Returns a `PersistedCredentials` with an initialized `Peers` map and zero-value server credentials (first-run / `FullReset` path). |
| `LoadCredentials` | `func LoadCredentials(outputDir, serverPeerName string) (*PersistedCredentials, error)` | Reads existing output configs from `outputDir` and extracts persisted credentials. |

### `LoadCredentials` behavior

| Situation | Return |
|---|---|
| Output dir or server config absent (first run) | `EmptyCredentials()`, `nil` — **not** an error. |
| Real I/O or parse failure of a present file | `nil`, wrapped error (`load server config for credentials: ...`). |
| Server config present | Server keypair **and** `HeaderProtectionKey` from its `[Interface]`; each peer's `PublicKey`/`PresharedKey`/`Name` from its `[Peer]`; each peer's `PrivateKey` recovered from its own `outputDir/<peer>/awg0.conf` (a client secret). |
| Server config missing, client directories present | Peer material is scanned from the client directories, but `HeaderProtectionKey` is **not** recovered — the next `Generate` generates a fresh key and every existing client config stops handshaking. |

The output tree is the credential store: keys exist only inside the generated INIs, so deleting `output/` silently rotates everything on the next run. `Generate` loads credentials from `opts.OutputDir`; when `OutputDir` is empty it always starts from `EmptyCredentials()`.

## EncodeVPNLink

| Symbol | Signature | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `EncodeVPNLink` | `func EncodeVPNLink(clientINI []byte, endpoint string, listenPort int, dns []string, description string) string` | Wraps a client AWG INI config into an AmneziaVPN-app-importable vpn:// link. Returns a `vpn://` URL string (scheme + base64url-encoded payload). |

`EncodeVPNLink` encodes a zlib-compressed JSON envelope (Qt-style `qCompress` with a 4-byte big-endian length prefix) as base64url without padding. The `last_config` JSON carries the verbatim INI (in `config`, for display) and structured fields (`client_priv_key`, `server_pub_key`, `allowed_ips`, `Jc`, `I1`, etc.) that the app's connect path reads. I1–I5 CPS tag strings are preserved verbatim, not expanded.

- `description` is copied verbatim into the envelope's `description` field (`json:"description,omitempty"`) — there is **no** hostname fallback. The pipeline passes the peer's `display_name`.
- Under AWG 3.x, the nine transport-protection keys (`HeaderProtectionKey`, `ContentPaddingAddition`, `RekeyAfterTime`, `RekeyTimeout`, `RejectAfterTime`, `KeepaliveTimeout`, `MaxHandshakeAttempts`, `RandomTrailers`, `DisableCookies`) are copied into `last_config` under their INI key names — but only inside the Jc-gated obfuscation branch, so a Jc-less config loses them. Pre-3.x links simply omit the fields; the app ignores unknown keys.
- The link is importable by the AmneziaVPN app, not by the standalone AmneziaWG app.

::: warning
`EncodeVPNLink` panics if `json.Marshal` fails for `lastConfig` or the outer envelope. This should never happen with valid input but is a theoretical crash path. No error-returning variant exists.
:::

See [VPN Import Links](/vpn-links) for the full wire format, field semantics, and AmneziaVPN-app compatibility notes.

## Helpers & iptables

| Symbol | Signature | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `IsValidIPAddr` | `func IsValidIPAddr(ipaddr string) bool` | `true` for a parseable CIDR string. |
| `ExtractSubnet` | `func ExtractSubnet(ipaddr string) string` | Network address plus prefix length; returns the input unchanged when it is not CIDR. |
| `GenerateRandomPort` | `func GenerateRandomPort() (int, error)` | `crypto/rand` port in `[10000, 65535]`. |
| `DetectMainInterface` | `func DetectMainInterface() string` | First non-loopback, up interface with at least one address; `""` when none. |
| `FindNextAvailableIP` | `func FindNextAvailableIP(serverAddress string, existingIPs []string) (string, error)` | Scans host parts `.2`–`.254`, skipping `existingIPs`; returns `""` with a nil error when nothing is free. |
| `GeneratePostUp` | `func GeneratePostUp(tunName, mainIface, subnet string, clientToClient bool) string` | IPv4 `iptables` setup rules joined with `"; "`. |
| `GeneratePostDown` | `func GeneratePostDown(tunName, mainIface, subnet string, clientToClient bool) string` | The same IPv4 rules with `-D` instead of `-A`. |
| `GeneratePostUp6` | `func GeneratePostUp6(tunName, mainIface, subnet string, clientToClient bool) string` | IPv6 `ip6tables` setup rules. |
| `GeneratePostDown6` | `func GeneratePostDown6(tunName, mainIface, subnet string, clientToClient bool) string` | IPv6 teardown rules with `-D`. |

## Library gotchas

| Concern | Behavior |
|---|---|
| Findings from `Generate` have no location | `GenerateResult.Findings` come from validating an in-memory config, so `Location.File`/`Line` are empty. For keyed rule codes (FLD/HDR/HPK/TRL/TRM) `Finding.OneLine()` renders a double space; keyless findings (PSC*/JNK001) carry no `Location` at all and render without any location or key segment (e.g. `[ERROR PSC002]: packet size collision (junk-range): ...`). `validate` re-stamps the path. |
| `AnalyzeOptions.Rand` is dead | Declared but never read; `analyze --seed` does not make reports reproducible. |
| `ProjectDir` / `JpathDirs` are inert | `GenerateOptions` stores both but `Generate` never reads them; use `LoadManifest(dir, jpathDirs)`. |
| `minS` is a breaking change | `GenerateSPrefixes` and `GenerateSPrefixesWithS1` gained a leading `minS` parameter in the 3.x work. Pass `0` for 2.0 and `12` under header protection. |
| Zero `Version` = AWG 2.0 output | A hand-built `ServerObfuscationConfig` with the zero `AWGVersion` emits exactly the 2.0 key set. |
| Preset → config loses the HP key | `Preset.ToServerObfuscation` leaves `HeaderProtectionKey` empty and the writer omits empty keys. |
| Asymmetric reuse | Key material persists across runs; every unpinned obfuscation parameter is re-drawn from `crypto/rand` on every call. |
| Non-atomic writes | `Generate` builds every config in memory first (all-or-nothing compute), but the disk-write pass uses `os.WriteFile` per file (mode `0600`) — a crash mid-pass can leave partially-written output. Use `SaveServerConfig` for atomic single-file writes. |
| Sorted peer iteration | Client peers are iterated alphabetically; when `PeerFilter` is set, only the named peers are built. Output ordering is deterministic. |
| Pointer nil ⇒ random | `ObfuscationManifest` uses `*int` / `*HeaderRange` so "set to 0" ≠ "unset". `nil` triggers random generation in `resolveObfuscation`. |
| Explicit 0 S is re-drawn | `fillMissingSPrefixes` keeps only non-zero S values (`pickNonZero`), so `{"s1": 0}` becomes a generated value. `jc: 0` survives only when `jmin` and `jmax` are both explicit. |
| `ServerPeerName` panics | Returns the sole server peer name but **panics** when count ≠ 1. Use `ServerPeer()` first, or call only on validated manifests. |
| `DerivePublicKey` panics | Panics on invalid base64 or non-32-byte input — no error return. Callers handling untrusted input must `recover` (or use the unexported `tryDerivePublicKey` helper which returns `""` on panic). |
| `GenerateKeyPair` / `GeneratePSK` / `GenerateHeaderProtectionKey` panic | Panic only on `crypto/rand` failure. Extremely unlikely but can crash the calling process. No error-returning variant exists. |
| `EncodeVPNLink` panics | Panics on `json.Marshal` failure for `lastConfig` or the outer envelope. Theoretical only — no error-returning variant. |
| Error wrapping | Failures are wrapped with `fmt.Errorf("<context>: %w", err)` (e.g. `resolve obfuscation: %w`, `load credentials: %w`, `build server config: %w`, `write file %s: %w`) — unwrap with `errors.Is` / `errors.As`. |
| Version enforced only by loaders | `LoadManifest` / `LoadManifestFromFile` reject any `version` other than `1`; a hand-built `Manifest` with `Version: 0` is accepted by `Generate`. |
| Missing manifest vs missing output | `LoadManifest` errors when no manifest file exists, while `LoadCredentials` returns empty credentials for a missing output directory. |
| `Manifest.ServerPeer` name order | With `count > 1` the returned name is arbitrary map order; only a validated (count == 1) manifest yields a meaningful name. |
| Protocol constants | `ProtocolQUIC`, `ProtocolDNS`, `ProtocolDTLS`, `ProtocolSTUN`, `ProtocolSIP`, `ProtocolRTP`, `ProtocolRandom` are the exported constants for `AnalyzeOptions.Protocol` and `PeerManifest.Protocol`. Prefer `amnezigo.ProtocolQUIC` etc. over bare string literals; use `ListProtocols()` to enumerate all valid values. See [Obfuscation](/obfuscation). |
| `PaddedSizes` ordering | Takes four separate ints (not an `SPrefixes` value) and returns init/response/cookie/transport — `148+S1`, `92+S2`, `64+S3`, `32+S4`. |
| Unknown CPS tags count 0 bytes | `ds`/`dz`, `c` and any malformed tag silently contribute nothing to `CPSLength`; `GenerateCPS` performs no collision avoidance. |
| Output layout | Configs are written as `<OutputDir>/<peer>/awg0.conf`; the INI/metadata structure is documented in [Output Format](/output-format). |
---
url: /gotchas
---
# Gotchas & FAQ

Amnezigo's sharp edges, collected in one place: mistakes that produce confusing
errors, behavior that does not match intuition, and the validation traps that
catch hand-edited configs. Entries are grouped by the kind of mistake and
ordered inside each section by severity — data loss and silent client breakage
first, correctness traps next, ergonomics last. Each entry states the symptom,
the consequence, and the fix, and links the dedicated page for the full model.

Several traps only appear on the **second** run: credential reuse,
header-protection-key persistence, the output overwrite, and the obfuscation
re-draw. A first run against an empty `output/` hides all of them.

::: warning Only four commands exist
`amnezigo init`, `add`, `edit`, `remove`, `export` and `list` were removed, and
there is no `Manager` API. The only commands are `generate`, `validate`,
`analyze` and `version`. Anything that still describes the removed commands is
stale. For the AWG 3.x feature set, the refreshed references are `README.md`,
the `docs/*.md` set and this `docs/llms-full.txt`; `AGENTS.md`, `docs/roadmap.md`
and `docs/plans/**` were not updated for it (`roadmap` and `plans` are
historical by design), so re-verify their 3.x claims against the code.
:::

## Common Mistakes

### Missing or wrong `version`

`version` must be exactly `1`. The field has no `omitempty`, so `{}` decodes to
`0` and an omitted field fails loading; any other value is rejected too.
Loading aborts before generation runs.

- Version `0` or omitted → `missing or zero version field`
- Version `99` → `unsupported schema version 99 (expected 1)`
- A Jsonnet manifest must emit `version: 1` in its output object, not a
  Jsonnet-level version.

**Fix:** start every manifest with `"version": 1`. The check lives in the
JSON/Jsonnet loaders; a `Manifest` built in library code with `Version: 0` is
accepted by `Generate`.

### Treating `"s1": 0` as a pin

Every numeric obfuscation field (`s1`-`s4`, `jc`, `jmin`, `jmax`, `keepalive`,
and the `h1`-`h4` range objects) is a **pointer**: omitting a key means "not
set" and the generator fills it, while writing a value means "use this". Zero
is special, though. `fillMissingSPrefixes` keeps only non-zero S values
(`pickNonZero`), so `{"s1": 0}` is **not** a pinned zero prefix — it is replaced
by a generated value. `"jc": 0` behaves the same way unless `jmin` and `jmax`
are both explicit (all three explicit short-circuits generation).

**Fix:** to randomize a field, leave the key out entirely. To pin it, write a
value — but S cannot be pinned to zero (a `0` is always replaced). `jc` can be
pinned to `0`, but only when `jmin` and `jmax` are also explicit; otherwise the
`0` is replaced like an S. Under header protection, pinned S values must be at
least 12 (see below).

### More than one server peer (or none)

A peer is a **server** only when it has *both* a non-empty `endpoint` **and** a
non-zero `listen_port`. A peer with just one of the two is a client; a client
that accidentally declares both becomes a second server. Exactly one server
peer is required; zero or more than one aborts generation with
`exactly one server peer required, found N` and writes nothing.

**Fix:** set `listen_port` only on the server peer, and check that no client
peer sets both `endpoint` and `listen_port`.

### A peer with no `address`

`address` is required, but neither the loader nor the pipeline validates it: a
blank address flows into the output as an empty `Address = ` line (and, on the
server side, an empty `AllowedIPs` for that client). The resulting config will
not come up. `validate` reports the condition as `FLD001`
(`required field "Address" is missing`) — but only for the file you point it
at. Duplicate addresses and colliding peer names are not checked either.

**Fix:** set an explicit CIDR on every peer — `/24` for the server
(`10.0.0.1/24`), `/32` for each client (`10.0.0.2/32`) — and diff `Address` and
peer names before handing out configs.

### Manifest fields newer than `awg_version` are hard errors

`header_protection`, `content_padding`, `rekey_after_time`, `rekey_timeout`,
`reject_after_time`, `keepalive_timeout` and `max_handshake_attempts` require
`awg_version` 3.0 or later; `random_trailers` and `disable_cookies` require 3.1.
Setting any of them under an older version fails generation with
`obfuscation.<field> requires awg_version <version> or later (got "<got>")` —
the fields are not silently ignored. The CLI wraps the message with
`generating configs: resolve obfuscation: `, and an invalid `awg_version` such
as `"3"` fails with `unsupported awg_version "3" (expected "2.0", "3.0", or
"3.1")`. The gate is on presence, not value: `header_protection: false` under
`"2.0"` is still an error.

**Fix:** raise `awg_version` or remove the field. Match the manifest to the
oldest engine in the fleet; see [Transport Protection](/transport-protection).

### Forgetting `network.mtu` collapses I1-I5 to `<t>`

::: danger Shipping defect — set `network.mtu` explicitly
Omitting `network.mtu` is a defect, not intended behavior. The emitted client
INI still says `MTU = 1280` (the default is applied afterwards), but CPS
generation reads the raw manifest MTU, which is `0` when the key is unset. The
max packet size goes negative, every template fails, and all five I-packets
fall back to the bare 4-byte `<t>` timestamp — the config keeps `MTU = 1280`
while losing all protocol mimicry. Verified live on a manifest without a
`network` section.
:::

**Fix:** set `network.mtu` explicitly in every manifest (1280 is the default).
See [Obfuscation](/obfuscation) for the I-packet templates.

### Pinning one `h` field does not pin the others

`h1`-`h4` are objects (`{"min": int, "max": int}`). Under header protection
with all four H fields omitted, the reference set `1-1`, `2-2`, `3-3`, `4-4` is
used. If even one H field is explicit, the other three are drawn from
`GenerateHeaderRanges()` — large ranges — and the explicit value is used
verbatim. A single `h1` therefore does not imply the rest of the reference set,
and mixed explicit/generated sets can overlap. Overlap is not detected by
amnezigo validation at all: the engine rejects it only when the config is
applied, with `headers must not overlap`.

**Fix:** pin all four H fields or none, and verify mixed sets against a real
engine. H ranges are always written two-part (`H1 = 1-1`); a bare `H1 = 7` in a
hand-edited config parses to `HeaderRange{}` silently.

### `header_protection: false` is not "plain 2.0"

It removes only the `HeaderProtectionKey` line. The six uint16 ranges and the
3.1 booleans are still emitted, and the H ranges switch from the reference
`1-1`..`4-4` set to large generated ranges (which `RISK007` will then flag).
With header protection off, the S floor of 12 is also skipped, so uniform S can
be drawn as low as 1.

**Fix:** for a 2.0-shaped config use `awg_version: "2.0"`;
`header_protection: false` is a half-disabled 3.x state, not a downgrade.

### Expecting `obfuscation.protocol` to select a template

The top-level `obfuscation.protocol` field is **dead configuration** — the
pipeline never reads it. Only the per-peer `peers.<name>.protocol` selects the
CPS template, and it defaults to `quic`. Unknown protocol names are not
rejected either: only the exact value `random` takes the random-tag path; any
other string, typos included, goes to the named-template path whose default
branch picks one of the six named templates at random.

**Fix:** set `protocol` on each client peer and spell it exactly (`quic`,
`dns`, `dtls`, `stun`, `sip`, `rtp`, `random`); ignore the top-level field.

### Two manifest files in the same directory

`LoadManifest` looks for `.amnezigo.jsonnet` first, then `amnezigo.json`. When
both exist, the **Jsonnet file wins and the JSON file is ignored** — no warning
is printed, so edits to `amnezigo.json` appear to do nothing. Only the exact
dot-prefixed filename is auto-discovered, and `LoadManifestFromFile` routes on
a case-sensitive `.jsonnet` suffix (`x.jsonnet.bak` is parsed as JSON and
fails).

**Fix:** keep exactly one manifest per project. Related loader traps: `--jpath`
**replaces** the implicit `<project>/lib` search path rather than appending to
it, relative jpath values resolve against the process CWD (not the manifest
directory), and duplicate imports resolve from the **last** `--jpath`
directory. Jsonnet has no external variables or TLAs (`std.extVar` fails with
`Undefined external variable`), and no Jsonnet library ships — `lib/` is a user
convention. See [Jsonnet](/jsonnet).

### Expecting a `preset` field

There is no `preset` key in the manifest and no `--preset` flag: presets are
copy-by-value data. Copying one also means copying its 3.1 knobs
(`content_padding`, `random_trailers`, `disable_cookies`) as well as its MTU
and default protocol, because the preset projection drops the latter two. The
uniform-S path requires `random_trailers` on **and** all four S values unset;
pinning any S disables it, so four of the seven presets (`home-balanced`
30/35/20/12, `mobile-aggressive` 60/60/50/24, `stealth-paranoid` 30/24/20/32,
`standard-1420` 32/28/20/16) always emit `TRL001` when `random_trailers` is on.
In the library, `ToServerObfuscation` hardcodes `Version: AWG31` — presets
carry no version field, so all of them are 3.1 data by construction.

**Fix:** copy the values from [Presets](/presets) by hand (or via your own
Jsonnet library), and either equalize S or set `random_trailers: false` if you
want a warning-free run.

## Surprising Behavior

### `generate` is not atomic on disk

The pipeline builds every file in memory first, so a *build* failure writes
nothing. The write loop itself is plain `os.MkdirAll(0750)` plus
`os.WriteFile(0600)` per file — no temp file, no rename, no rollback. An I/O
error or crash partway through leaves earlier files updated and later ones
stale. The library helper `writer.SaveServerConfig` does write to a `.tmp` file
and rename, but `Generate` never calls it.

**Fix:** re-run `generate` after any interruption instead of trusting a
partially updated tree. Treat `output/` as generated, not hand-edited.

### The output tree is the credential store

There is no state file. `LoadCredentials` recovers the server key pair and the
header-protection key from `output/<server>/awg0.conf`, and each peer's private
key from `output/<peer>/awg0.conf` — never from the server copy. A peer's map
key is both its name and its output directory (`output/<peerName>/awg0.conf`);
there is no `name` field inside a peer object. Deleting
`output/` or a single peer directory silently rotates the missing material on
the next run. If the server config is missing while client configs remain, the
fallback path never sets `HeaderProtectionKey`, so a fresh key is generated and
every existing client stops handshaking.

The peer **name** is the match key: renaming a peer looks like a new peer (new
directory, fresh keys), and a server config entry without a `#_Name` comment is
skipped, so that peer's key pair and PSK rotate on every run.

**Fix:** back up `output/` like a credential store; never delete peer
directories to "start clean." Use `--full-reset` when you want rotation.

### The header-protection key lives only in the server config

`LoadCredentials` recovers the key from the previous `server/awg0.conf`, and
`resolveObfuscation` reuses it only when it is non-empty and `--full-reset` was
not passed. Any run whose output has no 3.x key (`awg_version` `"2.0"`, or
`header_protection: false`) drops it from the persisted state, so the next 3.1
run generates a **new** key; every client still configured with the old key
stops completing handshakes. Live-verified: 3.1 → 2.0 → 3.1 rotated the key.
The key is also a plaintext, non-`#_` INI key duplicated in the server and
every client config, so anyone who can read a client config can decrypt
header-protected packet headers.

**Fix:** keep a given fleet on one `awg_version`; after any version-changing
run, re-import every client config. Treat client configs as secrets — they
already contain private keys. See [Credentials](/credentials).

### An empty server `PublicKey` line silently breaks every client

`resolvePeerCredentials` reuses the persisted server key pair verbatim —
private **and** public — with no re-derivation, unlike the client path, which
always re-derives. If `output/<server>/awg0.conf` has no `PublicKey` line, the
next run writes `PublicKey = ` (empty value, trailing space) into every
client's `[Peer]` section, with no error, no finding, and exit code 0. Verified
live.

**Fix:** never strip the server config's `PublicKey` line; check it after any
hand-edit. Recovery requires `--full-reset` or a fresh output tree.

### A corrupt `HeaderProtectionKey` blocks `generate` entirely

Any parse failure of the server config while loading credentials is fatal
(`load server config for credentials: ...`), and the parser rejects a header
key that is not 44-char base64 of 32 bytes. There is no fallback to
regeneration, so one bad line stops every subsequent run.

**Fix:** fix or delete the offending file. In the CLI the parse failure
surfaces as a `PSE001` finding; `HPK003` (the same condition as a finding)
fires only on an already-parsed in-memory config, so it is not what you will
see for a broken file.

### `--full-reset` is a fleet-wide re-provisioning action

The flag discards every persisted peer key pair, every PSK, and the
header-protection key. Every previously distributed config stops working with
the newly generated server config; without the flag, keys are reused.

**Fix:** treat `--full-reset` as a deliberate fleet-wide rotation, never a
local refresh.

### Key reuse is asymmetric: obfuscation is re-drawn every run

Persisted credentials are only the peer key pairs, the PSKs, and the
header-protection material. Every obfuscation field left unset in the manifest
is re-resolved from `crypto/rand` on each run: S1-S4, Jc/Jmin/Jmax, and the H
ranges — the H ranges only when header protection is off or H is partially
pinned; under header protection with all four H unset, the `1-1`/`2-2`/`3-3`/`4-4`
reference set is constant. Verified over six consecutive runs on the 3.1 fixture: keys
stayed byte-identical while `Jmin` varied 311-995 and S values came back 31,
31, 21, 17, 22, 23. Two consecutive `generate` runs therefore produce different
configs while all keys stay identical — and every client distributed from an
earlier run can no longer complete a handshake.

I1-I5 are recomputed per client per run too, but for named protocol templates
they are deterministic (same protocol + MTU ⇒ identical strings, reproduced
across runs); only `protocol: random` draws a fresh tag sequence each run, and
the on-wire bytes still differ on every connect because `<r N>`/`<t>` expand in
the engine.

**Fix:** pin every S/H/J value for byte-stable runs; otherwise re-import every
client after each `generate`.

### `--peer <one>` leaves every other client on stale obfuscation

The server config is always rebuilt with newly resolved S/H/J, while the peers
excluded by the filter keep the configs from an earlier run — and can no longer
handshake with the rewritten server. The filter is also silent about mistakes:
`--peer nobody` prints `Generated 1 config(s):` and exits `0`, and credential
resolution still loads every persisted peer.

**Fix:** omit `--peer` unless obfuscation is fully pinned in the manifest, and
verify peer names against the manifest before relying on the filter.

### `--dry-run` does not preview the keys a real run will write

Credential loading happens before obfuscation resolution regardless of
`DryRun`, so a dry run reuses the existing output tree when there is one (verified:
keys unchanged after a dry run) and falls back to fresh in-memory generation
when there is not. On a first run there is nothing to reuse, so the preview and
the following real run disagree — there is no way to preview exact keys.
`--dry-run` also prints the full file list including byte counts; the only
signal is the leading `Dry run — no files written` line.

**Fix:** use `--dry-run` to check structure and sizes, not keys; inspect the
files after a real run.

### 2.0, 3.0 and 3.1 emit different key sets for the same manifest

Under `"3.0"` the H ranges stay `1-1`..`4-4` and the header key, content
padding and timer ranges are emitted, but `RandomTrailers`/`DisableCookies` are
absent; under `"2.0"` none of the nine keys appear. Uniform S is only used when
random trailers are in effect (3.1) — so the drawn S values differ by target
version too. And `header_protection: false` does not produce a 2.0 shape
either (see above).

**Fix:** diff configs per target version; do not assume one manifest yields one
shape across versions. See [Transport Protection](/transport-protection).

### Older engines reject the 3.x keys, and 3.1 needs a 3.x runtime

The nine 3.x keys are unknown to 2.0/3.0 tools, which abort config loading with
`Line unrecognized`; the writer therefore gates emission on the resolved
version and emits nothing below 3.0. The generated 3.1 keys are engine
features, not config decoration: the shipped image pins
`amneziavpn/amneziawg-go:3.1.20260828`, and a 2.0-era userspace build or a
kernel implementation without the transport-protection layer cannot use them.
The "older engines reject the keys" claim rests on code comments and the
engine's own error string — the e2e suite only runs a 3.1 engine — so verify
against the runtime you actually deploy.

**Fix:** align `awg_version` with the oldest engine in the fleet and run an
AmneziaWG 3.1 userspace engine for 3.1 configs. See
[Installation](/installation).

### Client configs always emit `DNS = ` and `PersistentKeepalive = 0`

The client writer writes `DNS = ` with an empty value when `network.dns` is
unset, and always writes `PersistentKeepalive = 0` when the peer sets no
keepalive. The server writer omits both. Valid, but easy to mistake for a
rendering bug — and a server peer's `keepalive` field is silently ignored.

**Fix:** none needed. Set `keepalive` per client peer; the server config never
carries either line.

### Client `AllowedIPs` is always the full tunnel

`generate` hardcodes client `AllowedIPs = 0.0.0.0/0, ::/0`. There is no
manifest field for a split tunnel, and re-running `generate` overwrites hand
edits to the generated files.

**Fix:** for split tunneling, hand-edit or post-process the client config after
generation, and re-apply the change after every regeneration.

### `#_` metadata comments are load-bearing

The writer appends `#_EndpointV4`, `#_EndpointV6`, `#_ClientToClient`,
`#_TunName` and `#_MainIface` in `[Interface]`, and `#_Name`, `#_PrivateKey`
